name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean makes a Democratic win extremely unlikely
Incumbent Clay Fuller is running with strong outside support ($2.8M)
Prediction markets price Fuller at ~96% to win
Harris outraised Fuller heavily but spent it all, with little outside help
model.rationale: The R+19 lean and incumbent advantage make this a Safe R seat, and prediction markets agree at roughly 96% Republican. Harris's large fundraising total is notable but was spent down to almost nothing, with minimal outside backing, so it does not meaningfully move the forecast.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Harris within single digits, or a surge of outside Democratic spending, would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Georgia's 14th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 19 points to the GOP. Incumbent Clay Fuller returns after renomination, backed by roughly $2.8 million in outside support, while Democrat Shawn Harris has faced about $446,000 in outside opposition spending.

Harris has raised far more money directly than Fuller, but has nearly nothing left in cash and little outside help, suggesting early spending with limited late-war capacity. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and markets, which price Fuller at about 96%. The seat remains safely Republican.
